coupling.design: one plate per tray at its back right corner, facing out through the right-hand side; an actuated dock in the side wall of each slot a tray uses and of the bay; stroke 75 mm across the tray's travel; the plate's face 6 mm inside the tray's side

media.coupling: CT-E3-3 and CT-E3-2+PE, O3 mm, 39 A; PE mates first

coupling.why_not_the_back_edge: in a front-column slot and at the opening the back edge faces the shaft; a dock there would sit in the 106-146 mm between the tray and the extractor's platform, in the path of every tray it pulls, and at the opening the shutter is 35 mm behind the tray
sequence: shut and vent air, N2 and water (CombiTac: no mating or parting under pressure)
bay dock pushes in, pins first
contacts mate, supplies open, back on mains

sources.kardex_tray_power: #53: 'the trays will not retain power while in motion. They will only have power when stored, or again when they arrive at the delivery bay'; the dealer offered 'a quick connect cord' to the device on the tray. Kardex's own Shuttle option list shows no powered-tray or media option (kardex.com/products/vertical-lift/kardex-shuttle).
sources.combitac_align4: Staubli CombiTac uniq catalogue (CT-Main-11014009-en) p.80-81: CombiTac align 4, misalignment compensation radial 4 mm, angular +-2 deg; 100,000 mating cycles; the plug side's pins guide, the socket side is conical. p.82: 'the customer must provide a stable guide system, e.g. with mechanical pins'. p.87: largest gap between mated carriers 1-2 mm.
sources.combitac_power: CombiTac catalogue p.26: 'O 3 mm power unit up to 39 A', 600 V (pollution degree 2/CAT II).
sources.combitac_data: CombiTac catalogue p.46-49: 10 Gbit module, 'Ethernet up to 10 Gbit/s (Cat6a or higher)', RJ45 or M12 X-coded, 100,000 cycles, 14 N sliding force, 22 mm wide.
sources.combitac_air: CombiTac catalogue p.61-69: RCT06 pneumatic, 6 mm bore, shut-off on one side, 15 bar; 'Connecting and disconnecting under pressure is prohibited.'
sources.combitac_fluid: CombiTac catalogue p.70-75: SCT03 (G1/8) and LCT06 (G1/4), 'leakproof, shut-off on both sides', 15 bar; LCT06 8.48 L/min at 5 m/s, counter force 135 N at 10 bar; pressure drop 0.2-0.3 bar. Fluid couplings 'can also be used for pneumatic applications'.
sources.odu_dock: ODU-MAC Silver-Line P4+ docking frame: 'axial 1mm, radial +/- 4mm', floating, 100,000 cycles (ODU via adsgroup.org.uk).
sources.harting_dock: Harting Han 6 Mod Docking Frame 09140061716: floating +-2 mm, lock-in +-4 mm, >=10,000 cycles (harting.com).
sources.cpc_everis: CPC Everis BLQ6 blind-mate liquid coupling: Cv ~2.2, vacuum to 8.3 bar, 'disconnect under pressure without drips' (cpcworldwide.com; search snippet, page not opened).

unit.models: robot-arms PR #10 (branch claude/issue-239-20260926-2347), piper-camera-mount/cad/piper_mount.py: make_pi5_local (Pi 5 board, holes, connectors), make_hq_camera_local (HQ board, CS seat 14.43 mm, O36 back-focus ring, O34.8 housing, tripod mount and lock block off Raspberry Pi's drawing RP-008200-DS-1), make_cm_camera_local (Camera Module 3 board 25 x 23.862, housing 10.8, lens 8.3 mm proud); lenses.py: the 16 mm C-mount lens, O39 x 50 mm, 133.7 g, 22.2 x 16.7 deg on the HQ, with its 5 mm C-CS adapter.
unit.mount: robot-arms PR #40 (branch claude/issue-24-20261021-2053), docs/issue-24/camera-fixtures: 2020 posts in printed 90 x 90 mm feet with 50 mm sockets, wedges and Pi 5 plates on M5 drop-in T-nuts in the slot, a Camera Module 3 case on M2 standoffs, ribbon clips; one Pi per camera post, so a 200-300 mm ribbon is enough.

DAL #147: 1/4-20 insert to a bought arm rather than a printed ball joint; cameras within the 200/300/500 mm ribbons of the board.

adjust.height: block on the post's T-slot, two M5 drop-in T-nuts
adjust.pan: yoke on an M6 bolt through the block's arm, up to 75 deg each way
adjust.tilt: head between the yoke's arms, two thumb knobs, 15 deg up to 65 down

arm.note: reach.py's poses; the arm as capsules round its joint origins, the 2F-85 to the TCP

fov.hq_16mm: 22.2 x 16.7 deg: Raspberry Pi's figure for its 16 mm C-mount lens on the HQ Camera (robot-arms lenses.py)

views.method: the tray presented, the share of each camera's rectilinear picture (Wide 102 x 67 deg, HQ with the 16 mm lens 22.2 x 16.7 deg) whose rays leave through the opening into the room before they meet the tray's floor; nothing else counts as cover

docks_and_lift.method: every part as its bounding box (a lower bound on each gap); the extractor at every height from 0 to 3000 mm in 10 mm steps; each slide in 121 steps
docks_and_lift.walls: each dock's head passes through a window in its side wall (a column's perforated wall, or the bay's slatted one); the window takes out the tray supports 25-100 mm over the slot on that side, which only a tray stored in that slot would use

vlm.method: rise with no ventilation = W / (5.5 W/m2K x surface): the usual figure for painted sheet steel in still air, an estimate for a machine this size; airflow = W / (rho cp dT), air at 1.2 kg/m3 and 1005 J/kg K

vlm2.method: rise with no ventilation = W / (5.5 W/m2K x surface): the usual figure for painted sheet steel in still air, an estimate for a machine this size; airflow = W / (rho cp dT), air at 1.2 kg/m3 and 1005 J/kg K

ups.where: on every powered tray, back right, standing on its side in a bolted cradle (ups.py)
ups.transit_s: about 6 s from R2 to the opening: 2 x 1030 mm at 0.7 m/s (3 s), 246 mm at 2 m/s (0.1 s), plus the shutter and accelerations (not published); R4 adds about 0.8 s
ups.sizing: the smallest unit that carries the tray's backed branch at its rated draw and runs at least 10 min at its typical draw; heaters and big motors on the unbacked branch

n2.where: beside the VLM; N2 through the docks
n2.source: Parker Balston UHPN2-1100: 35 in H x 12 in W x 16 in D (889 x 305 x 406 mm), 50 kg (VWR), 120 VAC 60 Hz, 500-1100 cc/min at 99.9999 %, needs compressed air at 60-125 psig, no compressor of its own (govsci.com, gmi-inc.com, marshallscientific.com; search snippets). Peak Precision Nitrogen 1000: 1000 cc/min, 26 kg, no compressor (Peak's sheet, snippet).

chiller.heat_to_room: 900 W plus its own input, which was not found
chiller.where: beside the VLM; water through the docks, so its heat stays out of the enclosure
chiller.source: Thermo Scientific ThermoFlex 900: up to 900 W of cooling at a +20 C setpoint and 25 C ambient (60 Hz), 5-40 C, pump 15.1 L/min at 4.1 bar (thermofisher.com TF900, snippet). Its size and electrical input were not found.

ask_kardex: The heat a tray may give off in a slot, and in total, and the interior temperature the drives and controls are rated for.
Whether a column can be ventilated (a filtered fan and an outlet on the roof), and whether a furnace at 650 C may run inside at all.
The extractor's repeatability at a slot, for a dock that takes 4 mm of misalignment.
Whether the side walls can take a window and a dock behind the supports at a slot, and the space between the column wall and the cladding (about 108 mm in the model).
Whether power to a slot can stay on while a tray is stored, and what they would fit (the dealer offered a quick-connect cord).
